shop.title: Shop: Sahyadri Daily Needs, six branches
shop.summary: Daily sales of a grocery and household chain with six branches in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka, 1 January to 30 June 2026. Each sales row is one product's total for one branch on one day. Returns are recorded separately, in the returns table.

columns.branch_name: Short name used in the shop.
columns.opened_on: Date the branch opened. Hubballi opened in the middle of the period.

tables.name: products
tables.description: One row per product sold by the chain.

columns.current_price: Today's shelf price in rupees. Prices changed during the period; the price actually charged is in sales.unit_price.

tables.name: sales
tables.description: One row per product, branch and day: the quantity sold that day.

columns.unit_price: Price charged per unit that day, in rupees.
columns.amount: quantity times unit_price, in rupees, before any returns.

tables.name: returns
tables.description: Goods brought back by customers. Not subtracted in sales: net sales = sales.amount minus returns.refund_amount.

columns.sale_id: The sales row they were sold on.
columns.reason: Reason noted by the cashier. Often blank: cashiers did not always ask.

gaps: There is no customer information, so the data cannot say how many customers came or who came back.
There is no cost price, so the data cannot say which product or branch made a profit.
Nagpur has no sales rows for 10 to 12 April 2026. The data does not say whether the shop was closed or the records were lost.
Hubballi opened on 16 March 2026, so its totals cover a shorter time than the other branches.
Return reasons are blank for many returns.
try: Which branch sold the most in May?
Which branch sold the most in May, net of returns?
Which product made the most profit?
What were total sales of cooking oil each month?

school.title: School: Vaigai Higher Secondary School, classes 8 to 10
school.summary: Six classes (grades 8, 9 and 10, sections A and B) in an invented school in Madurai, academic year 2025-26 (June 2025 to March 2026): students, monthly attendance and marks in three exams.

tables.name: students
tables.description: One row per student. Names are invented.

columns.gender: F or M, as recorded at admission.
columns.joined_on: Date the student joined. Some joined after the year began.

tables.name: attendance
tables.description: One row per student per month, only for months after the student joined.

columns.school_days: Days the school was open that month for this student.
columns.days_present: Days the student was present. Compare students with days_present / school_days, not raw counts.

columns.max_marks: Marks each paper is out of. The unit test is out of 25, the others out of 100.

tables.name: marks
tables.description: One row per student, exam and subject.

columns.subject: English, Maths or Science.
columns.marks: Marks scored. Blank (NULL) when the student was absent for that paper; blank is not zero.

gaps: No reason is recorded for any absence, so the data cannot say why a student missed school.
Blank marks mean the student was absent. The data does not say whether a re-test happened.
There is nothing about families, income, travel or health, so the data cannot explain why marks differ.
Students who joined late have fewer months of attendance and may have missed the first exam.
The data does not say who taught each subject.
try: Which class had the best attendance in December?
What was the average Maths mark in the Half-yearly exam by class?
Why did grade 9B do worse in Science?

clinic.title: Clinic: Periyar Community Clinic, Kochi
clinic.summary: Out-patient appointments with five doctors at an invented community clinic in Kochi, January to March 2026. Each row is one appointment or walk-in visit, with the booked, arrival and seen times.

columns.clinic_days: Days of the week the doctor sees patients here. One doctor comes only twice a week.

tables.name: appointments
tables.description: One row per appointment or walk-in visit.

columns.patient_code: Invented patient code; the same code means the same patient.
columns.visit_type: booked (appointment made earlier) or walk_in (no appointment).
columns.arrived_time: Time reception marked the patient as arrived. Blank if the patient never came.
columns.seen_time: Time the doctor called the patient in. Blank if the patient was not seen.
columns.status: seen, cancelled (by the patient, in advance) or no_show (booked but never came).
columns.wait_minutes: Minutes from arrival to being seen. Blank unless the patient was seen. It is not how late the doctor ran: early arrivals wait longer.

gaps: No reason is recorded for cancellations or no-shows, so the data cannot say why patients did not come.
There is nothing about the patient (age, illness, distance), so the data cannot explain who waits longer or why.
The data does not record how long each consultation took or when it ended.
Reception rounded times to the nearest 5 minutes.
try: What was the average wait for each doctor in February?
What share of booked appointments were no-shows?
